$comment: Domain summaries. A cluster is a human-facing grouping of micro-topics; the graph, not the cluster, is the source of truth for ordering. Colours are chosen to stay legible against both the light and dark page background.

clusters.name: The loop, in Claude Code's hands
clusters.subject: Claude Code in Action
clusters.summary: The same agentic loop as everywhere else in this graph, but run by the CLI on your actual files and terminal: the Explore → Plan → Code → Commit workflow that gives each phase of the loop a name, and the habit of a fresh subagent reviewing the diff before it lands.
clusters.notesPart: What Claude Code is · Explore → Plan → Code → Commit

clusters.name: Matching control to risk
clusters.subject: Claude Code in Action
clusters.summary: The six permission modes as a risk spectrum, what Auto's classifier actually checks (intent, not correctness), when plan mode earns its keep over direct execution, and the two techniques — the interview pattern and the Explore subagent — that make plan mode's discovery phase safe to trust.

clusters.name: CLAUDE.md that Claude follows
clusters.subject: Claude Code in Action
clusters.summary: What CLAUDE.md actually is — guidance loaded into every prompt, not enforced configuration — the four stacking locations, @import for sharing conventions across packages, .claude/rules/ for path-scoped conventions, and the phrasing habits that keep a growing file from drowning out its own best rules.
clusters.notesPart: CLAUDE.md — the basic model · A CLAUDE.md that Claude actually follows

clusters.name: The right mechanism for the rule
clusters.subject: Claude Code in Action
clusters.summary: The three-way split that runs through the whole section — durable context in CLAUDE.md, reusable procedures in a Skill, unskippable enforcement in a hook — plus the concrete surfaces that split maps onto: shared vs. personal slash commands, skill frontmatter, and the verification skill worth building first.
clusters.notesPart: Verification skills · Put each rule in the right mechanism

clusters.name: Steering a long session
clusters.subject: Claude Code in Action
clusters.summary: The habits that keep a multi-hour session legible: /compact with a direction versus /clear's clean slate, the rewind menu's five checkpoints, /goal and /loop for work that spans turns, and worktrees for running parallel sessions without their file changes colliding.

clusters.name: Hooks: deterministic enforcement
clusters.subject: Claude Code in Action
clusters.summary: The event lifecycle a hook can attach to, the exit-code contract that decides whether Claude even sees the objection (and the exit-1 trap that catches almost everyone once), the PreToolUse permissionDecision field, and updatedInput's whole-object replacement for rewriting a call instead of blocking it.

clusters.name: MCP and tool design in the CLI
clusters.subject: Claude Code in Action
clusters.summary: Where an MCP server is scoped (local, user, or project via .mcp.json), the context-cost tax every configured server pays whether or not it's used, the 10%-of-context threshold that flips Claude Code into tool search mode, and why Claude Code's own toolset stays generic instead of hyper-specialized.
clusters.notesPart: MCP and Hooks — the basic model · MCP inside Claude Code

clusters.name: Routines, headless, and plugins
clusters.subject: Claude Code in Action
clusters.summary: The three ways to run Claude Code without someone watching each turn — a managed Routine, a headless -p invocation, or the Agent SDK — the flags that make headless output machine-parseable, managed Code Review versus the GitHub Action, and what a plugin actually bundles.
clusters.notesPart: Automating repeat work · GitHub Actions and Code Review · Plugins

clusters.name: Trusting an unsupervised run
clusters.subject: Claude Code in Action
clusters.summary: Verifying in proportion to how little you watched, turning a promise into a gate with a Stop hook, why a cold second opinion catches what the original session rationalized past, and the seven-step evidence checklist that ties the whole section together.
clusters.notesPart: Trust it: verifying unsupervised runs · Verification and trust
